findings.title: add_members silently ignores usernames with surrounding whitespace
findings.body: The controller splits params[:usernames] on ',' and looks each piece up with User.find_by_username without stripping whitespace. The user-selector component produces a comma-separated list, and users commonly type 'alice, bob' with a space after the comma; ' bob' will not match any user and is silently skipped, so the admin believes members were added when they were not. Strip each username (e.g. usernames.split(',').map(&:strip)) before lookup.

findings.title: remove_member deletes the join row but never saves the group, so the removal is not persisted
findings.body: group.users.delete(user_id) issues a DELETE against the group_users join table directly and returns the number of rows deleted; it does not modify the in-memory association in a way that group.save would persist, and more importantly the subsequent `if group.save` only saves group attribute changes — the membership deletion has already been executed (or, depending on association caching, may be lost when the association is reloaded). The spec passes only because it reloads and the DELETE already hit the DB, but the code is misleading and fragile: if the DELETE affected 0 rows (user not a member) the endpoint still returns success_json, and the save call is dead weight. The method should check the delete result and return an error when the user was not a member, and should not rely on group.save for a membership change.

findings.title: add_members reports success even when no usernames matched or the group failed to save members
findings.body: The action adds users via group.add(user) (which only mutates the in-memory association) and then calls group.save. If none of the supplied usernames exist, or group.save fails to persist the membership for any reason, the response is still success_json when save returns true (save succeeds because no group attribute changed). There is no feedback to the admin about which usernames were ignored. At minimum, unknown usernames should be reported back (the old PATCH implementation had a test asserting silent success for non-existent users, but silently dropping input in a bulk-add endpoint is a data-integrity risk for admins).

findings.title: update uses Group.find which raises RecordNotFound (500) instead of a 404 for unknown ids
findings.body: Group.find(params[:id].to_i) raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound for a missing group, which Rails turns into a 500-level error page in production rather than a 404. The same pattern exists in destroy (line 50), add_members (line 66) and remove_member (line 85). Use Group.find_by(id: ...) and render a 404, or rescue RecordNotFound, so clients get a correct status code.

findings.title: members endpoint has no upper bound on limit, enabling expensive full-table scans / large payloads
findings.body: limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i is used directly in .limit(limit) with no maximum clamp and no validation that it is positive. A caller can pass limit=100000000 (or a negative value, which in some ActiveRecord adapters disables the LIMIT clause entirely) and force the server to serialize every member of a large automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0, everyone) in one request, a trivial denial-of-service vector. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. [limit, 100].min) and reject non-positive values.

findings.title: offset is not validated and negative offsets produce undefined SQL behaviour
findings.body: offset = params[:offset].to_i is passed straight into .offset(offset). A negative offset generates invalid SQL on PostgreSQL (OFFSET must be >= 0) and raises a 500. Validate offset >= 0 (the Ember client already clamps with Math.max(offset, 0), but the endpoint is public and must not trust clients).

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when the group has no name, breaking promise chains
findings.body: When the group name is empty the method executes `return ;` (undefined) instead of returning a resolved promise. Callers such as admin_group_route.js setupController (`model.findMembers()`) and group-members.js.es6 call it without chaining today, but the previous implementation returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) precisely so callers could chain. Any current or future `.then()` on the result will throw TypeError: Cannot read property 'then' of undefined. Restore `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]);` (or Discourse.ajax-compatible resolved promise).

findings.title: findMembers clamps offset against a stale user_count, allowing out-of-range offsets and wrong pagination state
findings.body: offset is computed as Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0)). On the first call user_count is the default 0, so the clamped offset is always 0 regardless of the requested offset — fine initially, but after members are removed the stored user_count shrinks while this.get("offset") may still point past the end; the clamp uses the old total, so the server returns an empty page while the client believes it is showing page N. Worse, the server response then sets offset from result.meta.offset, but the request was already sent with a bogus offset. The clamp should be against the server-reported total after the first fetch, or simply trust the server to handle out-of-range offsets and let meta correct the state; as written it can permanently wedge pagination after membership changes.

findings.title: removeMember and addMembers hit /admin/groups/:id/members.json but routes define member actions under the group resource without .json and without an id segment matching the client URL
findings.body: The client calls '/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json'. The routes added in config/routes.rb are `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` inside `resources :groups`, which generate /admin/groups/:group_id/members (DELETE/PUT). Two mismatches: (1) the client appends .json — Rails will still route this because the format segment is optional, so this works, but (2) the controller reads params.require(:group_id), which matches the route's :group_id segment, so that part is consistent. However the client sends the group's numeric id in the URL while the controller's other actions use params[:id]; this is fine, but the spec for remove_member (spec line 115) issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` — a PUT to remove_member — while the route only maps DELETE to remove_member. The test passes only because controller specs bypass routing. The real client uses type: "DELETE" which matches, but the test does not exercise the actual route/verb combination, so a verb mismatch would ship undetected. Fix the test to use the correct HTTP verb (delete) and verify routes with a routing/request spec.

findings.title: next action can advance offset past the last page when user_count is not a multiple of limit
findings.body: offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count")). If user_count is 120 and limit is 50, the last valid offset is 100, but this formula allows offset to become 120 (min(100+50, 120)), requesting an empty page; totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 = 3, so currentPage becomes floor(120/50)+1 = 3 and showingLast is true, masking the bug, but the request for offset=120 returns zero members and the UI shows an empty member list on the 'last' page. The clamp should be Math.min(offset + limit, Math.max(user_count - limit, 0)) or rely on the server meta to correct offset.

findings.title: save error handler assumes e.responseText is valid JSON and .errors is an array
findings.body: var message = $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors; will throw if the response body is not JSON (e.g. a 500 HTML error page or an empty body) or if errors is a string, producing an unhandled exception inside the rejection handler and leaving disableSave stuck... actually .finally resets it, but the bootbox.alert never shows and the error is swallowed into an uncaught TypeError. Guard the parse (try/catch or check e.responseJSON) and fall back to a generic message.

findings.title: each over members uses itemView="group-member" but the view/template naming may not resolve, and members is set asynchronously
findings.body: The template iterates `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. The view is defined as an ES6 module default export in admin/views/group-member.js.es6 with templateName "admin/templates/group_member". In this Ember version, string itemView lookup resolves against the global namespace (Discourse.GroupMemberView), not the ES6 module registry, so the custom view (and its "item" class used by the .ac-wrap .item CSS) may never be applied, falling back to a default item view. Additionally, members is populated asynchronously by findMembers() called in setupController; before the first response the each renders nothing, which is acceptable, but there is no loading/empty state. Verify the view actually resolves (e.g. register it globally or use the resolver-compatible naming) — otherwise the remove button styling/behaviour relies on a view that may not exist.

findings.title: members template iterates `members` but the group-members route sets the model to the group and members are loaded onto the group object, not the controller
findings.body: The route (group-members.js.es6) sets controller.set("model", model) where model is the Group, then calls model.findMembers() which sets `members` on the Group model. The template `{{#each m in members}}` looks up `members` on the controller (the template's context), not on the group model. Unless the controller proxies unknown properties to the model (ObjectController proxying was removed/changed depending on Ember version — this route's controller is a plain controller, not ObjectController), `members` will be undefined and the list will always be empty. The template should iterate `model.members` (or the route should set controller.set('members', ...) after findMembers resolves). Also note the stray `` on line 19 with no matching opening tag inside the each block, which produces invalid HTML.

findings.title: Stray closing tag inside the each loop
findings.body:
Line 19 contains `` but there is no corresponding opening
within the each block (the opened on line 7 is closed on line 18). This produces malformed HTML; browsers will hoist the stray close tag, potentially breaking the table layout. Remove it.

findings.title: addMembers does not clear the usernames input after adding (acknowledged TODO)
findings.body: The action calls this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames")) but never resets this.set("usernames", null). The TODO comment acknowledges it. Consequence: after a successful add, the user-selector still shows the previously entered usernames; clicking Add again re-submits the same list (harmless but confusing), and combined with the silent-skip behaviour in the controller for unknown users, the admin gets no feedback. Clear the property in the model's addMembers .then() or in the action.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT but the route only accepts DELETE, so the test does not match production behaviour
findings.body: The spec issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` and `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` in the other test. Controller specs bypass routing, so the PUT test passes even though config/routes.rb maps only `delete "members"` to groups#remove_member. A request-spec or routing assertion is needed; as written, if the route verb and the client verb ever diverge (the client uses type: "DELETE"), no test will catch it. Also the first test expects 422 for group_id 1 (an automatic group) but never verifies the member was NOT removed when the group is non-automatic and the user_id does not exist — remove_member returns success even when nothing was deleted (see controller finding).

findings.title: add_members spec does not cover whitespace-separated usernames or unknown usernames
findings.body: The spec only tests the happy path with a clean comma-joined list and the automatic-group rejection. Given the controller splits on ',' without stripping (see controller finding), a test with "user1, user2" (space after comma) would fail today. Add a test for usernames with surrounding whitespace and one asserting behaviour (ideally an error or per-username feedback) when a username does not exist.

findings.title: members response shape changed from a bare array (render_serialized) to {members, meta}, a breaking change for existing API consumers
findings.body: Previously the endpoint returned render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer) — a top-level JSON array. It now returns { members: [...], meta: {...} }. Any existing client (including older cached JS, third-party API consumers, or the previous version of the Ember model which did result.map(...)) will break because result is no longer an array. The Ember model was updated in the same PR (result.members.map), so first-party code is consistent, but this is still a public API contract break that should be called out in the PR description and ideally versioned or kept backwards compatible.

findings.title: Search parameter interpolated into ILIKE with wildcards unescaped, allowing wildcard injection
findings.body: groups.where("name ILIKE ?", "%#{search}%") interpolates user input into a LIKE pattern. A search containing % or _ acts as a wildcard (e.g. search=% matches all groups). This is a minor issue (the endpoint is admin-only and only lists group names), but it also means a search for a literal '%' cannot be performed and results may be unexpectedly broad. Escape LIKE wildcards in the search term (e.g. using ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like if available, or gsub).

findings.title: setupController calls findMembers on every entry but never resets offset, so returning to a group shows a stale page
findings.body: The Group model persists `offset` as instance state. Navigating away from a group (e.g. after paging to page 3) and back reuses the same Group object from the adminGroups model list (model hook finds it by name in the already-loaded collection), so findMembers() is called with the old offset and the admin lands on page 3 instead of page 1. Reset group.set('offset', 0) in setupController (or in the route's model/afterModel) before calling findMembers.

findings.title: asJSON no longer wraps attributes in a `group` key, but create/save send it as top-level params while the controller reads top-level params — verify create actually persists alias_level
findings.body: asJSON returns { name, alias_level, visible } at the top level, and create/save POST/PUT that as request params. The controller's create action reads params[:name] and params[:visible] but never sets alias_level on create — so a newly created group always gets the default alias_level (0) even if the UI selected another value; the value is silently dropped. The update action does read params[:alias_level]. Either the controller's create must also assign alias_level (group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?), or the UI must issue a follow-up update. As written, creating a group with a non-default alias level loses that setting.

findings.title: create does not validate or reject duplicate group names explicitly, relying on model validation error rendering
findings.body: create builds a Group with the given name and calls save; if the name is a duplicate the model validation fails and render_json_error group returns the errors — this is handled. However there is no test covering duplicate-name creation or invalid names (spaces, etc.), and the client's save error handler (admin-group.js.es6 line 85) does $.parseJSON(e.responseText).errors which assumes the errors key exists. Add a spec for duplicate name creation to lock in the error contract between server and client.

findings.title: Member routes are nested as member actions on resources :groups, producing /admin/groups/:group_id/members, but the client also appends .json and the controller uses params.require(:group_id) — confirm the format segment does not break the require
findings.body: The client requests '/admin/groups/123/members.json'. Rails parses the .json as the format, so params[:group_id] is still '123' and params.require(:group_id) succeeds. This works, but it is fragile: if the route were defined with an explicit format constraint or if the client URL were built differently (e.g. /members.json/123), it would break. More importantly, the route helper names (remove_member_admin_group_path etc.) are not used anywhere; consider using explicit `member do delete :members ... end` with as: naming or documenting the URL contract. Low severity because it functions, but the mismatch between the client's hardcoded URL construction and the resourceful route is worth a comment or a shared constant.

findings.title: findMembers is fired without awaiting, and the public members page has no pagination UI despite the endpoint now supporting limit/offset
findings.body: The public group members page calls model.findMembers() which requests only the first 50 members (model default limit: 50) and the template renders all of `members` with no pagination controls. Previously the endpoint returned all members (up to 200 for automatic groups); now large groups (e.g. trust_level_0 with thousands of users) will silently show only the first 50 members on the public page with no way to see the rest. Either add pagination to the public page or keep the public route requesting a larger limit. This is a functional regression for group member browsing.
